channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Dysphoric Flesh" - Currently seeking feedback from all, but esp. trans users

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
Summoned by PM

I'm not going to do an LBL on this just now because I have a queue to get through - if you'd like one let me know and I can try and do one next week.

I enjoyed this. There is a really… uncomfortable sense to the progression here. On some level, I feel genuinely a little gross about reading the story of this person's suffering, knowing what will happen the whole way through, and just having it happen without being able to do anything about it. That being said, it's the kind of uncomfortable and gross that works, I think, largely because of the fact that it's clearly framed as such.

I've considered saying that the ending is a little flat, but I don't think there's a solid way to change that which wouldn't also make the article overall feel just a bit too uncomfortable? I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. The ending is a little less climactic than it could be, I think, but it's not bad. Like WarFang said, it's a relief to see Lief is okay, and that might be enough on its own.

I think the voice constructed for Lief could be a little more… distinct? It's not bad, but it doesn't feel particularly unique and given the emotional and narrative core of the article is built around those diary entries, and therefore Lief's voice, it could do with being a bit more compelling in my opinion. Give the reader more to latch onto, and it will make the overall arc even more involving and engaging.

Otherwise, I think this is a solid piece of writing. Well done, and I wish you the best of luck with it.

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
drops in time 4 thoughts

+ smells like brain
- thonk

Preface: I am a trans person, but it goes without saying that my own thoughts don't stand for the whole, and I'd still recommend seeking out more willing trans/nb critters.

Okay SO, I read the first(?) iteration of this originally about a week+ back, and I can definitely say that some of my original opinions have changed for this article.

At first - and this was very much a more personal gripe, mind you - I really wasn't…feeling it, y'know? It was a pretty solid draft but initially it wasn't necessarily to my tastes.

This is no longer much the case, though.

The addition of the diary excerpts definitely makes this, for me - it's a perfect touch of a human element I didn't realise that the original iteration was lacking. The slow creep of dread and anguish that you build up through it is, truth be told, viscerally uncomfortable but in the way that's reflective of good, solid writing - as a transmasc person specifically I felt that shit in my soul.
(Moreover the fact Leif was okay and this wasn't gonna end up being a more tragic example of the anomaly's effect was a huge relief tbh)

I still do hold this worry about this anomalisation of the concept of dysphoria, in the context of trans and nb people, though perhaps a little less now. Moreover I did not think my stance on that would change, but lo, here we are.

I don't think I really have much negative to say beyond the personal concerns I've laid out abane this paragraph. You took a solid working draft and you made it into a good draft, in my opinion, capturing perfectly the reality and horror of what it's like to deal with dysphoria. Furthermore, it doesn't feel like the article is forcing the idea that dysphoria has to be to particular severity.

I look forward to seeing where this goes. It certainly is interesting.

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
+ Open for critique
- Behold!

Preface: I am not a trans person, my critique is not going to be about the potential sensitivity of the article as I am not a good source to judge how it will affect trans people.

My opinion on this right now is that it's somewhat hollow as well as overlong. There is some horror imagery here, specifically:

When SCP-XXXX-2’s head has become engulfed, direct respiration, as well as the direct consumption of food and drink, becomes impossible. SCP-XXXX will provide SCP-XXXX-2 with an intravenous supply of oxygen, nutrition, and hydration, however the amounts supplied are suboptimal for survival.

and

This sheath grows from the attachment site at the back of the neck, over the head, and eventually covers the entire body. SCP-XXXX’s underdeveloped eye and mouth structures move to the front of SCP-XXXX-2’s head and become enlarged. Upon completion of this process, SCP-XXXX is considered to have entered its adult phase.

I do like the ending, but yet it feels hollow at the same time. I believe this is because the entirety of this article is a cold description of the anomaly and what it does. Not that these types of descriptions don't work, more that it's the issue at hand should be explored on a more personal level. If I'm reading this correctly, SCP-XXXX is the embodiment of transphobia, dysphoria, and self-hate. A cold, clinical description doesn't really convey that in a meaningful way.

My advice is to cut everything after the bulleted list and have the article pivot to either interview logs with an SCP-XXXX-2 instance. These would serve to show how SCP-XXXX functions on -2 while also providing the audience with a connection to this character. The ending you also have would have a bit more punch to it if we see these Foundation doctors supporting this character and their gender identity

cybersqyd recommended reaching out to more reviewers and I have to agree with ver on that.

Good luck!

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

I find the image of a trans person physically slicing the embodiment of transphobia from themselves to be very powerful, and the final line is basically the closest this thing can have to a happy ending. I'm wondering, do you have any suggestions for making that final paragraph more impactful or obviously important to the metaphor?

The problem here is that making it land better feels like it's…a lot more likely to feel jarring? Really though, my issue is more that the ending feels…not climactic enough? And I'm not sure how to make this feel more climactic tbh without leaning more into the darkness. This said: it might just be my natural inclination towards darker writing that's coming through here rather than an objective truth.

I did consider this, but decided against it as really, these aren't parasites as we understand them but are rather the embodiment of the gender that people feel a trans person should have. Therefore, their ultimate purpose is to totally usurp the host like a cuckoo bird, not to propagate.

Like, I get this and accept your reasoning for this but it feels, to me, a little too loose and up in the air without the propagation; but at the end of the day, this is your call.

I'm not sure how to incorporate it or trim it, although it seems important for thematic purposes that it remain in some form.

It'd work better if there was some additional connection here; where like, -1 is the only one who can affect which way -2 goes but it feels…too much like that'd be putting everything on one person when really it's everyone that affects stuff. Honestly, I don't think it really adds much and I'd just trim it completely if you're not going to e.g. tie it into the end cycle or something instead.

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
Follow up questions
wow you opened the box

but it feels…like the ending just kinda…happens?

It's important to me for multiple reasons that whatever other changes are made, The nature of the final paragraph remains. I find the image of a trans person physically slicing the embodiment of transphobia from themselves to be very powerful, and the final line is basically the closest this thing can have to a happy ending. I'm wondering, do you have any suggestions for making that final paragraph more impactful or obviously important to the metaphor? I don't want readers to gloss over it by taking it too literally.

it feels, like you'd have this great opportunity for like…the SCP-XXXX instance to crumble into dust and emit more parasites

I did consider this, but decided against it as really, these aren't parasites as we understand them but are rather the embodiment of the gender that people feel a trans person should have. Therefore, their ultimate purpose is to totally usurp the host like a cuckoo bird, not to propagate.

like, the -1 instances really like…come together to crow about how good a job they did protecting their kid from being trans and like, regretting that being trans killed their kid

This is a good idea, but I can't think of a way to do it that isn't too heavy handed or takes away focus from the ending. Further advice would be appreciated.

I'm also kinda iffy about this starting in the mother at all as a thing; it feels…underutilised?

This is very fair. Originally the piece was going to be all about mothers, but as the scope of the metaphor expanded it fell by the wayside. I'm not sure how to incorporate it or trim it, although it seems important for thematic purposes that it remain in some form.

I…am hesitant only in that this feels…miserable?

I am very interested to hear some thoughts about how I could intensify the glimmers of hope that I want to end the piece with.

Thanks for some great crit.

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
Oops I forgot I had placeholdered this yesterday until I went to bed but I have uh just managed to not go over 24hrs too much

[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I'm a little conflicted on this as a whole: the final few paragraphs have this really delightful rising sense of dread that works for me in a really dark way that I really dig; but it feels…like the ending just kinda…happens? I was originally going to highlight this just appearing in wombs as being an issue:

SCP-XXXX may manifest in the wombs of women who have undergone menopause and are the parent of adult children who currently identify as transgender or non-binary

But I think it could be worked better into the ending: it feels, like you'd have this great opportunity for like…the SCP-XXXX instance to crumble into dust and emit more parasites and have like, the -1 instances really like…come together to crow about how good a job they did protecting their kid from being trans and like, regretting that being trans killed their kid while the narrative here is very framed around the mothers being more responsible?

It's a hard balance: in some ways, the ending resulting in more spread of this feels like it'd be more narratively satisfying but it also feels like it might really impact the kinda…broad impact that it currently has; where like, at the moment it affects basically every trans person. But I feel like the specific horror might outweigh that: in that, having it feel like a kinda localised, spreading phenomenon would help make this feel more real and hence more impactful?

I'm also kinda iffy about this starting in the mother at all as a thing; it feels…underutilised? Like a lot of the horror comes more from peoples reactions to this happening to -2, and so it feels like the instances originally being from the mother feels almost tangential?

There's some pacing issues: it kinda feels like the start of the description drags stuff out a lot in a very dry way; and it feels more concisely moving to the actual meat of this would land better.

There's a small part of me that feels like this needs more than a light touch up at the end: I can see like, a longer form diary or series of interviews say having a much larger effect here; but it feels like they might really struggle to show anything new that the description already implies, and I don't necessarily think having a big focus on a specific mother/child relation here would actually be the best way to do this.

Speaking here from a sensitivity perspective alone: I don't think this has issues with that specifically; though there's definitely points where it feels like this is going to be really bad in that regard. I think tying the detransitioning stuff into people's reactions, and in turn, the eventual death into exclusively people being unsupportive works. I…am hesitant only in that this feels…miserable? It's very much a piece about despair and the loss of hope and while I personally think that it's done in a way which works, I can see people disagreeing and I would suggest reaching out to a few other trans/non-binary critters about this.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

openly transgender and non-binary individuals for signs of SCP-XXXX activity.

I'm, not necessarily a fan of 'signs of SCP-XXXX activity' here: on the one hand, keeping it open for any kind of sign like this is probably good for ConProcs; but it feels like this is a really great moment for you to imply something specific to hook a reader in; perhaps 'for signs of parasitic infection by SCP-XXXX' or perhaps something more specific.

SCP-XXXX is then to be surgically removed from SCP-XXXX-2 and stored in isopropyl.

I feel like either "The SCP-XXXX instance…" or "All the SCP-XXXX instances…" would work better here; really emphasise that there's not just one SCP but a whole host of them, y'know?

is not conducive to healthy function

something about 'healthy function' feels really odd here; it feels weirdly dehumanising and I'm not sure whether that's good or not?

Due to global and regional disparities in access to and quality of healthcare for trans and non-binary people, as well as the social capability for such individuals to be open about their identity, detection of SCP-XXXX activity is difficult.

Part of me wonders whether explicitly mentioning webcrawlers and social media here would be a good idea but I think this is fine?

including a long prehensile tail and a segmented anatomic structure.

SCP-XXXX is equipped with a jawless, toothed mouth and four hooklike claws on its underdeveloped appendages. Instances have been recorded to reach lengths greater than 0.4 meters.

I can't quite put my finger on why; but something about this flow feels iffy? I wonder whether moving the 'greater than 0.4meters' to a footnote after 'enlarged' would help?

It's possibly that this is the first time you mention 'instances' or the repetition of sentences starting with 'SCP-XXXX' being broken this way is a little jarring but I'm not sure.

Analysis has shown SCP-XXXX to be genetically identical to humans.

This feels…iffy; 'humans' feels like an overly broad thing for 'genetically identical' to work since like two humans can be relatively genetically different? I wonder whether specificity would help here: are they genetically identical to their host? To one specific human?

These subjects, hereby referred to as SCP-XXXX-1

It feels odd to have a -1 but not have anything in the ConProcs relating to it

is sleeping. it then makes its way to offspring of SCP-XXXX-1 in proximity.

missing capital; and ending on 'in proximity' feels like it's missing a noun (like, in that, it's implied you mean 'in proximity to -1' but the construction feels iffy cos there's no explicit thing saying that); and also feels vague; perhaps tying the 'travel up to a kilometer' line in here would work better instead of having it in the next sentence?

SCP-XXXX will attach itself to offspring of SCP-XXXX-1 that identify as transgender or non-binary

'identify' feels odd here: it kinda implies that a) people who aren't trans but identify as can be affected and b) people who are trans but don't identify as such can't be affected and I wonder whether just saying 'offspring of -1 that are' would be better?

SCP-XXXX does not feed on SCP-XXXX-2 directly.

This feels a little weirdly placed right now: it's kinda mentioned in passing in the middle of a paragraph, but the idea of feeding isn't touched on more for like…two, large paragraphs more, and so it feels like perhaps it'd work best just before the "SCP-XXXX is thought to feed on positive attention paid to…." sentence?

However, the perceived appearance of SCP-XXXX-2 will differ from their actual pre-exposure appearance in multiple ways. These inconsistencies mimic the secondary sexual characteristics of the sex assigned to SCP-XXXX-2 at birth, as well as non-genetic traits stereotypically associated with that sex by the culture of the subject observing SCP-XXXX-2.

This section, and the rest of the paragraph it's in, feels…like it uses a lot of words to not say a lot: the dense, clinical tone feels like it doesn't setup a very evocative image of the transformation. I feel like perhaps trimming down the list of alterations a little, and perhaps mentioning a few examples might convey this more evocatively but it might be hard to get the examples to feel right here.

If SCP-XXXX-2 possesses a chosen name different from the name given to them at birth, they will become unable to pronounce it.

Does this apply if they meet someone else using the name? I guess this isn't fully a critique so much as me wondering whether this has much larger scale impacts than intended?

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
CW/TW: Discussion of trans trauma, dysphoria, and suicide, by a trans individual.

http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/oystershell Look under the "Dysphoric Flesh" "Brood of my Brood, Skin of my Skin" "Usurper" tab.

This is a story about what truly horrifies me most. In case it's not clear, I'm trans myself.

While anyone and everyone's thoughts and critiques are welcome, I am especially keen on receiving feedback from other trans and non-binary folks.

EDIT 1: Draft 2 is now up. Draft 2 contains revised ConProcs, a slew of small edits and revisions to the Description including addressing almost all of cybersqyd's LBL's, and the addition of a reproductive system for the SCP. Still looking for feedback on sensitivity, as well as critique on the overall narrative and flow, as well as advice on how to stick the landing if the current ending is underwhelming for you. Also added an image and revised the title.

EDIT 2: I've created an alternate version, Available under the "Their Eyes Don't Cry" tab. I've cut down the description to just the bare minimum, and have finished the article off with two case files in order to provide more of the human element. Even with the cuts, it's more than twice as long as "Brood of my Brood" and I'm quite unsure about parts of it. Regardless, please let me know which version you prefer and which should get my attention as I continue to revise.

EDIT 3: After some careful consideration, I've decided to go with the long ending, but I've cut it and re-written it entirely. It's shorter now and I'm happier with the quality. Let me know what you think.

Thanks in advance.
